Error.description: The single JSON document written to stdout when a command run with --output json fails, and the body of a failed REST or MCP operation. Exactly one of this or a success document is emitted. Codes are stable: renaming one is a breaking change. The full registry is in docs/ERRORS.md and in the capabilities manifest.

causes.description: Additional errors of the same shape when several independent problems were found at once, as when a configuration has many invalid fields. The top-level error summarises them.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier. Branch on this, never on the message.

column.description: 1-based column in the source file, when known.

details.description: Further structured context, shaped per code. Never contains secrets or response bodies.

exit_code.description: Exit code the CLI used or would use for this error: 2 usage, config or policy refusal; 3 preflight or runtime failure; 4 run invalid; 5 wait timed out.

hint.description: What to do about it, concretely. Present whenever a fix can be named.

line.description: 1-based line in the source file, when known.

message.description: One sentence describing what went wrong, in lower case and without a trailing period.

path.description: JSON Pointer to the offending location in the input document, when the error is about a document.

retriable.description: Whether repeating the identical call could plausibly succeed. Configuration and policy errors are never retriable.

run_id.description: Run this error belongs to, when it happened inside a run.

Error.title: TracePoint error envelope

info.description: Correlated HTTP, SQL and Redis load testing that reports which tier a slowdown came from. Every operation is also an MCP tool with the same name, input and output.
info.title: TracePoint

post.description: Return the safety policy this server enforces: which targets may be loaded, whether writes and destructive statements are allowed, rate, concurrency and duration ceilings, and how many runs may be active at once. Call it before writing a configuration so the configuration fits, and when a call is refused with a POLICY_* code. The policy was fixed by a human when the server started; no call can change or exceed it - report a refusal to the human rather than working around it.

policy.description: The safety envelope every call is held to. A configuration can tighten it but never exceed it.

how_to_change.description: Who can change it and how. An agent cannot.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Return the compact, prioritised summary of a finished run: validity, SLO outcome, the verdict with evidence and confidence, the worst incidents, headline numbers per tier, machine-applicable recommendations and artifact paths - in that order. Read it before anything else and stop when you have the answer. A recommendation with action rerun carries the exact overrides to pass to start_run. Correlation is not causation; say so when reporting.

budget_chars.description: Largest digest to return, in characters (default 4000). When content is dropped to fit, truncated is true and more says what to fetch with get_run_section.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Return one page of one section of a finished run's result: incidents, per-label summaries, the per-bucket timeline of a runner, telemetry samples, or capacity levels. Use it only when the digest is not enough - when it was truncated, or to check the evidence behind a verdict in a specific time window. Pages keep each response small.

section.description: incidents: every incident in full. labels: per-label summaries. timeline: per-bucket numbers for one runner. telemetry: samples from one sampler. levels: capacity-search levels.

runner.description: For timeline, the runner (default: the application runner). For telemetry, the sampler: generator, postgres, mysql or redis. For labels, restricts to one runner.

from_s.description: For timeline and telemetry, the start of the window in seconds from the run start.

to_s.description: For timeline and telemetry, the end of the window; 0 means the end of the run.

200.description: Get one section of a run's result

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.summary: Get one section of a run's result

post.description: Return a run's state without waiting: pending, running, completed, interrupted, aborted, failed or lost, with progress, heartbeat and exit code. Use wait_for_run instead when you want to block until it finishes.

run_id.description: A run id from start_run or list_runs; a unique prefix or suffix of one also works.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: List runs newest first with status and exit code. Use it to find a run_id, or to see whether a run is already active before starting another - only one test should load a target at a time.

limit.description: At most this many runs, newest first (default 20).

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Describe exactly what a run would do - offered load per runner, targets, SLO budgets and the effective safety envelope - without contacting anything. Call it before start_run to confirm the load and the targets are what the human agreed to.

config.description: The configuration itself: a YAML string, or the same document as a JSON object. Give this or config_path, not both. tracepoint schema config describes every field; scaffold_config writes a starter.

config_path.description: Path to a configuration file, relative to the directory the server was started in. Give this or config, not both.

overrides.description: --set style overrides applied on top, as path=value; list items are addressable by name, as in db.queries[by-id].weight=5. A digest's recommendations carry these ready to use.

200.description: Plan a run without running it

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.summary: Plan a run without running it

post.description: Render a finished run as Markdown, JUnit XML or the offline HTML report, from its result.json, and write it into the run directory. Use markdown to post a summary on a pull request or in a CI job summary; use html to hand a human the full report (every run already writes report.html, so this only re-renders it). For deciding what to do next, read get_run_digest instead: it is smaller and carries the recommendations.

format.description: markdown (default): a summary sized for a pull-request comment or CI job summary, returned inline. junit: JUnit XML whose failures match the exit codes, returned inline. html: the offline report for a human, written to the run directory; only its path is returned.

path.description: Where the report was written, inside the run directory.

content.description: The report itself, for markdown and junit. Absent for html, which is for a person to open, not for a model to read: give the human the path.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Write a commented starter configuration for an application and, optionally, the database and Redis it uses, probing each storage tier alongside the application so a slowdown can be attributed. It can infer these from a project directory (detect_dir) and import requests from an OpenAPI document (openapi_path). Use it when there is no configuration yet. It contacts nothing. Ask the human which targets and environments are allowed and what the SLOs are before running anything it produces.

base_url.description: Base URL of the application under test, such as http://127.0.0.1:8080. Use an environment reference like ${BASE_URL} to keep hosts out of the file. Required unless detect_dir is given.

paths.description: Request paths to load, such as /api/items. Safe (read-only) endpoints only unless a human has said writes are fine. Defaults to /.

db_driver.description: Database to probe alongside: postgres, mysql or sqlite. Omit for none.

db_dsn_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the database DSN, such as DATABASE_URL. The file references it; the value is never written.

redis_addr_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the Redis address, such as REDIS_ADDR. Omit for no Redis probe.

rate.description: Application requests per second. Defaults to 20; start low and raise it once a smoke run is valid.

duration.description: Run length as a Go duration, such as 30s or 3m. Defaults to 30s.

db_query.description: The database probe's query. Defaults to SELECT 1, which sees the connection but none of the application's tables; a read the application itself performs is a far better probe.

detect_dir.description: A project directory, relative to the server's, to infer the rest from: compose files for the database, cache and application port, environment files for variable names (never values), and an OpenAPI document for the requests. Explicit inputs win over what is detected.

openapi_path.description: An OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document, relative to the server's directory, to import requests from: safe methods only, with generators for path parameters and TODOs for anything uncertain. Needs base_url, because a document's servers often name production.

config_yaml.description: A commented starter configuration. Pass it to validate_config, then plan_run, before start_run.

notes.description: What the starter assumed and what to check.

inferences.description: What detection concluded from the project directory, each with its evidence and a confidence of high, medium or low. Confirm the low ones with the human.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Validate, preflight and start a run in the background, returning its run_id at once; load tests outlive tool calls. Configuration errors, policy refusals and preflight failures are returned synchronously, before any load. Then call wait_for_run until it finishes and read get_run_digest. Start with a short smoke run (30s) and only run one test against a target at a time. It generates real load against the targets.

config.description: The configuration itself: a YAML string, or the same document as a JSON object. Give this or config_path, not both. tracepoint schema config describes every field; scaffold_config writes a starter.

config_path.description: Path to a configuration file, relative to the directory the server was started in. Give this or config, not both.

overrides.description: --set style overrides applied on top, as path=value; list items are addressable by name, as in db.queries[by-id].weight=5. A digest's recommendations carry these ready to use.

seed.description: Seed for every random choice; recorded in the result. Reuse a run's seed to reproduce it.

allow_invalid.description: Resolve an invalid run to exit 0 instead of 4. Almost never what you want: an invalid run measured the generator, not the target.

run_id.description: Pass to wait_for_run, get_run_status, get_run_digest and stop_run.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Ask a running test to stop. It stops offering load within half a second, drains in-flight work and writes a partial result marked interrupted, which wait_for_run then returns. Use it when a run is no longer wanted or is hurting a target; stopping an ended run does nothing.

run_id.description: A run id from start_run or list_runs; a unique prefix or suffix of one also works.

stopped.description: True when a stop was requested; false when the run had already ended.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Load and validate a configuration under this server's policy without contacting anything. Every problem is reported at once, each with a stable code, a JSON path, a line and a fix. Call it after writing or changing a configuration and before plan_run or start_run.

config.description: The configuration itself: a YAML string, or the same document as a JSON object. Give this or config_path, not both. tracepoint schema config describes every field; scaffold_config writes a starter.

config_path.description: Path to a configuration file, relative to the directory the server was started in. Give this or config, not both.

overrides.description: --set style overrides applied on top, as path=value; list items are addressable by name, as in db.queries[by-id].weight=5. A digest's recommendations carry these ready to use.

effective.description: The configuration after defaults, with secrets redacted.

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.description: Wait up to timeout_s seconds (at most 50) for a run to finish. Returns finished=false with the current state if it is still going - call again - or the final state, exit code and digest when done. Read the digest's validity first: an invalid run measured the generator, not the target, and its verdict must not be reported.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait in this call, 1 to 50 seconds (default 45). If the run is still going when it expires, call again.

finished.description: True when the run reached a final status. False means it is still going: call wait_for_run again.

exit_code.description: The run's exit code, once finished: 0 valid and within budget, 1 budget breached, 3 failed or cut short, 4 invalid.

digest.description: The run's digest, once finished - the same document get_run_digest returns.

200.description: Wait for a run to finish

default.description: A coded error; branch on error.code, never on the message.

post.summary: Wait for a run to finish
